Fit an unpenalized smooth modified DLNM knots_depriv <- quantile(dataset$depriv, probs = c(0.10,0.90))  model3 <- dlnmLPS(dtot ~ factor(dow) + sm(depriv, arg = list(type = "ns", knots = knots_depriv)) +                         sm(basis.max_pen, arg = list(pen = 2),                            by = depriv, arg.by = list(type = "ns", knots = knots_depriv)) +                         sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +                         sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +                         sm(District, arg = list(type = "ind")),                    data = dataset,                    offset = log(pop),                    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE, CPO = TRUE),                    family = "Poisson") # Fit a penalized smooth modified DLNM model4 <- dlnmLPS(dtot ~ factor(dow) + sm(depriv, arg = list(type = "ps", df = 5, pen = 2)) +                         sm(basis.max_pen, arg = list(pen = 2),                            by = depriv, arg.by = list(type = "ps", df = 5, pen = 2)) +                         sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +                         sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +                         sm(District, arg = list(type = "ind")),                    data = dataset,                    offset = log(pop),                    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE, CPO = TRUE),                    family = "Poisson") # Calculate counterfactual attributable risk depriv_lower <- round(quantile(data2007_district$depriv, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),2) af2007_counter <- attributable_risk(   basis = basis.max_pen,    cases = data2007_district$dtot,    model = model4,   cen = 25,   x = data2007_district$Tmax,   by = rep(depriv_lower, length(data2007_district$depriv)),   group = data2007_district$District,   dir = "back",   tot = TRUE,   samples = TRUE) # title: Introduction to dlnmLPS
text: dlnmLPS package provides tools fitting Distributed Lag Non-linear Models (DLNMs) (Gasparrini et al. 2010) within Bayesian framework. DLNMs can require estimation large number basis coefficients represent complex exposure-lag-response relationships. Penalized DLNMs provide flexible way model relationships, still avoiding overfitting (Gasparrini et al. 2017). However, fitting penalized DLNMs can computationally demanding large number model coefficients. Consequently, unpenalized DLNMs often used practice. dlnmLPS addresses computational challenge exploiting Laplace approximations, allowing unpenalized penalized DLNMs estimated efficiently within Bayesian framework. approach allows fast estimation accounting uncertainty model parameters. vignette provides introduction basic functionality dlnmLPS (Rutten et al. 2026). first demonstrate install load package, fit basic DLNM without penalization. subsequently show type model can fitted using penalized splines. advanced modelling options demonstrated separate vignettes (see vignette("spatially-varying-dlnms"), vignette("effect-modified-dlnms") vignette("joint-dlnms")).

Note , default, additional lag penalty specified, top P-splines penalties, encourage shrinkage towards null effect longer lags. disable penalty, specify add.lagpen= “FALSE” within arg argument.
